## `state.json` → `project` no longer depends on how the repository was cloned (#64)

Since 0.23.0 `project` falls back to the repository name when `context/workflow.json` names no `project` and
no active roadmap does. That name came from `origin`'s URL in the clone's letter case, so a checkout of
`owner/repo_name` and one of `owner/REPO_NAME` disagreed: the doctor reported `state-stale (project)` on one of
them, and a regenerated file turned the next pull request red for a change it did not make.

- `npx softure-skills state` (`context_state.py write`, also `--staged`) writes the repository name into
  `context/workflow.json` → `project` the first time it falls back to it, in the spelling `state.json`
  already holds. From then on the name is fixed in the repository. A `workflow.json` with unstaged edits is left
  alone under `--staged`. `context_state.py pin-project` does only this step.
- The installer does the same on install and update when the project has `context/` and nothing names it.
- Until the name is pinned, the doctor compares a repository-derived `project` without regard to letter case,
  and a rewrite keeps the committed spelling. In GitHub Actions the forge's spelling (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) wins
  over the clone URL when both name the same repository.

Adopting projects: set `project` in `context/workflow.json` once (or run `npx softure-skills state` and commit
the pinned name). WORKFLOW.md §12.4 lists it as step 0 of the rollout.

### How it was checked

A project between roadmaps without `project`, `state.json` written from `https://github.com/acme/Clinic-Site.git`,
then checked out from `https://github.com/acme/clinic-site.git`:

| Step | 0.24.0 | 0.25.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `context_state.py check` (the doctor's `state-stale`) | fails: `project` | passes |
| `context_state.py write` from the lower-case clone: `state.json` → `project` | `clinic-site` (changed) | `Clinic-Site` (unchanged) |
| `context/workflow.json` → `project` after that write | absent | `Clinic-Site` |
